legal_contingencies.composition_note: Primarily European Commission (EC) fines, in addition to accruals related to other legal matters and regulatory fines and settlements.

reasonably_possible_loss_in_excess_of_ac.note: No aggregate reasonably-possible-loss-in-excess-of-accrual dollar figure located for Alphabet. The accrued $15.6B is a recorded liability, NOT a reasonably possible loss estimate.

legal_contingencies.verbatim_quote: As of December 31, 2025, we had short-term accrued legal and regulatory fines and settlements of $15.6 billion. This amount primarily included EC fines, in addition to accruals related to other legal matters and regulatory fines and settlements.

individual_matters.note: Per-matter amounts (individual EC fine amounts, specific settlements) were not extracted in this pass; only the aggregate accrual is asserted as ground truth.

reconciling_items.label: Alphabet-level activities
reconciling_items.note: Unallocated corporate costs; includes AI-focused shared R&D, corporate initiatives, charges/fines. Presented as a separate line, not a reportable segment.

reconciling_items.label: Hedging gains (losses)
reconciling_items.note: Appears in the revenue build only, not the operating income build.

traps: Hedging gains/losses is a revenue-build line with no operating-income counterpart — easy to double count or mis-map.
Alphabet-level activities is a negative reconciling item, not a segment; including it in 'segments' inflates segment_count to 4.
Google Services total (342,721) is a subtotal above finer revenue categories in the same table; grabbing both double counts revenue.

long_term_income_taxes_payable.note: Primarily related to unrecognized tax benefits; timing/amount of payment cannot be estimated. This is NOT the 'would affect ETR' figure.

traps: Long-term income taxes payable of $9.5B (line 890) is a balance-sheet classification figure and is frequently mistaken for the 'UTB that would affect the effective tax rate'.
Reconciliation is presented in BOTH dollars and percent across three year-columns; column mis-alignment silently yields FY2023/FY2024 values.
'Changes in unrecognized tax benefits' is a rate-reconciliation line and is distinct from the UTB rollforward table.
